slot.brief: Two rods of same material but different lengths and radii conduct heat between the same temperatures; compare thermal resistances or heat currents.

stem: Two cylindrical rods of the same material connect the same pair of temperatures. Rod A has length $L$ and radius $r$, while rod B has length $2L$ and radius $2r$. What is the ratio of their heat currents, $H_B/H_A$?

verdicts.working: Heat current is proportional to cross-sectional area divided by length. Thus, H_B/H_A = (4A/2L)/(A/L) = 2.

working:
$H=\dfrac{k\pi r^2\Delta T}{L}$
$\dfrac{H_B}{H_A}=\dfrac{(2r)^2/(2L)}{r^2/L}=2$

Independent check: Heat current is proportional to cross-sectional area divided by length. Thus, H_B/H_A = (4A/2L)/(A/L) = 2.
solution:
For heat conduction, $H=\dfrac{kA\Delta T}{L}$, so for the same material and temperature difference, $H\propto \dfrac{r^2}{L}$.\\
$$\dfrac{H_B}{H_A}=\dfrac{(2r)^2/(2L)}{r^2/L}=2$$
